subject: gk
question: Article 171 deals with ________.

options.text: qualifications of the Chief Minister of a State
qualifications of the Governor of a State

solution:
The correct answer is __**composition of the Legislative Councils**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 171** of the Indian Constitution deals with the **composition of the Legislative Councils**.
 
• The Legislative Council is the upper house in those states of India that have a bicameral legislature.
 
• According to Article 171, the total number of members in the Legislative Council of a state shall not exceed one-third of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that state.
 
• The members of the Legislative Council are elected by various groups including the Legislative Assembly, graduates, teachers, and local authority members.
 
• The Governor of the state also nominates some members to the Legislative Council.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 168** of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of the Legislative Council in states.
 
• The creation or abolition of the Legislative Council in a state can be done by Parliament on the basis of a resolution passed by the Legislative Assembly of the state.
 
• Currently, six states in India have a Legislative Council: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The Legislative Council is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution, but one-third of its members retire every two years.
